chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Vinson's band: personnel, Savoy, Apollo and Dinah Washington
summary: The band was a full orchestra with bassist Theodore Swain, played the Savoy, Apollo and the road, and Dinah Washington sang with it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, who was in Cleanhead's band?
Let's see, it's two of the guys on here. What's his name? I know Clarence Strauss wasn't. Sparrow, this trombone plaver. (Nick Sparrow--ed.)
Oh?
And --
Was it a full band?
It was a full band, yes.
Well, who was playing piano on bass and with you?
With Eddie Vinson? Vincent?
Yeah.
I'll tell you that in a few minutes. She knows exactly who it was.
Yeah, all right. Who was the bass player?
Theodore Swain.
I don't know him.
Well, he played bass with Cootie's band.
Did he?
Yes.
Uh-huh.
Very good bass player. He's dead, also.
Well, so you were playing the Savoy?
Oh, yeah, I played the Savoy.
With -- Cleanhead had an engagement at the Savoy.
Yeah, we had an engagement at the Savoy and the Apollo Theatre. We went out on the road.
Were you when you were with Mo Caleb?
Right. See, he put the band together, see.
Yeah.
And --
I see.
-- We had a singer, was Dinah Washing-ton. She came in, she was singing with the band.
Who found her?
A little girl that sang with Earl Hines. Little short --
Madeleine Green --
HEMLOCK
No, no, no, no. What's her name? Pretty little girl. She had a real baby voice, like, when she sang.
This is before Sarah.
Before --
No, after Sarah Vaughan. After Sarah sang with Earl.
This was before Sarah sang with Earl Hines.
Peally?
Yes.
Oh, well, I don't remember. I'll ask Stan. He'll know. But, anyway, she recommended Dinah Washington?
Well, through Mo Gale.
Found her through her?
No, it was -- see, Dinah was with Fddie Vinson first.
Yeah.
And then she came in to replace Dinah Washington because Dinah was pregnant. That's what it was, see.
Oh, I see. Yeah.
That's the way that was.
Oh, I see. So this is the girl that was
Right.
Yeah, I see. Right, okay. So it was a good band, then.
Oh, it was a very good band, very good band. Eddie Vinson, Vincent, he had a very good band.
Yeah, very good band.
Very good band.
Who else did he have on reeds that you can remember?
I'd have to get the picture and show you. I can tell you --
That's all right. It takes -- sometimes things stand out in your mind that if you don't get out, you don't remember.
Yeah, I have to think of the guys' names.
Yeah.
Plus I have pictures of them. (it).
How long were you with him?
I was with him for about -- almost a year. Because I made a lot of his records with the band.
Oh, you did?
Yes.
